title: Cheapest Grading Company (2026)
verdict: The cheapest grading company for cards in 2026 is GMA at $9 a card on orders of 100, and AGS at $15 in bulk is the least expensive that grades by measurement.
A low fee only helps if you meet the conditions. With one card, GMA, CGC bulk and ISA are out, and the choice is Beckett at $14.95 and 45 business days or more, or AGS at $18 and 20 or less.

why: One price covers everything. $18 buys the scan, the grade, eight subgrades, the report and the slab, for any card at any value. Orders of 30 or more TCG cards pay $15 a card on the standard bulk tier.

You see why the card got its grade. AGS issues eight subgrades, four for the front and four for the back, plus a defect list and a 3D heightmap. Most graders hand back one number. A buyer who can open the report has less to argue about.

Bulk pricing starts at 30 cards, a low bar for a dealer. TCG cards are $15 each at 20 business days, $20 at 10 and $30 at 5, and sports cards are $3 more per tier. Every card in a bulk order still gets the full report and eight subgrades.

faq.q: What is the cheapest grading company?
faq.a: AGS at $18 for a single card with subgrades included, or $15 from 30 cards. CGC is cheaper at $10 if you have 10 or more cards worth under $500 each.

faq.q: What costs come on top of the grading fee?
faq.a: Shipping to the grader, return shipping and insurance, and supplies such as penny sleeves and card savers. Some graders add membership fees, subgrade fees or value upcharges. AGS adds return shipping at checkout.

faq.q: Is there a discount on a first AGS order?
faq.a: Yes. AGS lists code AGSNEW20 for 20% off a first grading order.

faq.q: Do graders charge more for valuable cards?
faq.a: Several do. PSA and SGC price by declared value, and CGC caps each tier by card value and moves a card up if it is worth more. AGS, Beckett, TAG and ISA say they add no upcharge for value.

faq.q: Is it worth grading a low-value card?
faq.a: Only if grading lifts the price by more than the fee plus shipping, or if you want the card protected and documented. At $10 to $18 a card the math works on far more cards than at $50.
